record.title: Diet-induced weight reduction when excess adiposity is relevant
record.proposition: In adults with obesity and insulin resistance without diabetes, approximately 5% diet-induced weight loss improved clamp-measured insulin sensitivity compared with weight maintenance.
record.capRationale: Existing D/B/P/R sum and ceilings applied; no extra replication decrement.

rationale.D: The randomised comparison directly measured the specified insulin-sensitivity endpoint with clamp/tracer methods.
rationale.B: Randomised maintenance comparator and stabilised weight before retesting; differential attrition, unmasked intervention and incompletely verified concealment limit protection.
rationale.P: Primary-outcome power calculation and dispersion reported; modest completer groups and outcome variability limit precision and generalisability.
rationale.R: One directly appraised exact 5% protocol. Later stages and secondary analyses of this cohort are not independent replication; other weight-loss protocols were not credited without full appraisal.

targetedChecks.access: Full PMC4833627 text: study design, clamps, statistical analyses and results inspected; Scite supplied abstract only.
targetedChecks.assessment: In adults with obesity and insulin resistance without diabetes, approximately 5% diet-induced weight loss improved clamp-measured insulin sensitivity compared with weight maintenance.

sources.contradictoryAssessment: Conditional obesity/insulin-resistance population; not a general weight-loss recommendation. The 5% phase did not reduce measured systemic/subcutaneous adipose inflammatory markers; mediation is unestablished. Greater weight-loss stages involved a smaller subset, not independent replication or a separately randomised dose comparison.

limitations: Conditional obesity/insulin-resistance population; not a general weight-loss recommendation.
The 5% phase did not reduce measured systemic/subcutaneous adipose inflammatory markers; mediation is unestablished.
Greater weight-loss stages involved a smaller subset, not independent replication or a separately randomised dose comparison.

record.title: Conditional oral arginine supplementation in the tested type-2-diabetes protocol
record.proposition: In the small lean type-2-diabetes study, one month of oral L-arginine 3 g three times daily increased clamp-measured glucose disposal but did not normalise it relative to healthy controls.
record.capRationale: Existing D/B/P/R sum and ceilings applied; no extra replication decrement.

rationale.D: The primary abstract directly reports the named oral exposure and clamp glucose-disposal endpoint.
rationale.B: Pending full methods: abstract describes randomisation and double blinding, but allocation, masking, exclusions and analysis safeguards remain unverified.
rationale.P: Pending numerical tables and statistical methods: percentage change alone cannot establish variance, between-group uncertainty or precision.
rationale.R: One directly identified exact protocol. No independent replication credited from citation counts or differently dosed studies.

targetedChecks.access: Primary abstract via PubMed and Scite; publisher HTML and original PDF returned403. No full-method verification claimed.
targetedChecks.assessment: In the small lean type-2-diabetes study, one month of oral L-arginine 3 g three times daily increased clamp-measured glucose disposal but did not normalise it relative to healthy controls.

retrievalLimited.limitation: Primary abstract via PubMed and Scite; publisher HTML and original PDF returned403. No full-method verification claimed.

sources.contradictoryAssessment: Twelve lean adults with type2diabetes; not a general supplement or food prescription. Glucose disposal remained below healthy-control values; cGMP change does not prove NO-mediated causality. Full methods and uncertainty estimates were inaccessible; B and P remain pending rather than assigned zero.

limitations: Twelve lean adults with type2diabetes; not a general supplement or food prescription.
Glucose disposal remained below healthy-control values; cGMP change does not prove NO-mediated causality.
Full methods and uncertainty estimates were inaccessible; B and P remain pending rather than assigned zero.
